channel.title: Brazil Elections 2026
channel.description: Real-time monitoring of the 2026 Brazilian presidential elections.

item.title: Ex-presidente do Rioprevidência diz à PF que aportes de quase R$ 1 bilhão no Master foram sugeridos por ex-diretor
item.description: The former president of Rioprevidência, Deivis Marcon Antunes, told the Federal Police that the R$970 million investment in Banco Master was proposed by the then investment director Euchério Lerner Rodrigues, and that he only signed off after the directorate's proposal. He denied receiving bribes or that his appointment was political, despite sources indicating influence from Antônio Rueda of União Brasil. The case involves alleged irregularities in investments made without internal committee approval.

item.title: Veja o que já se sabe sobre o novo programa para renegociar dívidas
item.description: The federal government is advancing the design of a new debt renegotiation program for households, aiming to replace old debts with new financing featuring lower interest rates and longer terms. The initiative responds to high household indebtedness and is one of President Lula’s priorities for the 2026 election year.

item.title: ‘Quem ganha em Minas leva o Brasil’: veja por que o estado é estratégico para a eleição de presidente
item.description: Minas Gerais is considered a key state in Brazilian presidential elections, as the candidate who received the most votes there has never lost the election since 1998. This is due to its regional diversity, which mirrors different profiles of Brazil — Northeast, Southeast, and Center-West — along with socioeconomic indicators similar to the national average. Although there is no scientific basis for the maxim, experts acknowledge its strategic value due to the representativeness of the Minas Gerais electorate.

item.title: Votos de condenação de Castro no TSE devem ser publicados até o fim de semana e podem destravar julgamento sobre eleição no Rio
item.description: The TSE is set to publish by the weekend the ruling that made former Rio de Janeiro governor Cláudio Castro ineligible for eight years due to abuse of political and economic power in the 2022 elections. The document is awaited by the STF to determine whether Castro’s resignation was legally valid or an attempt to evade the conviction, which will decide if Rio’s elections will be direct or indirect.

item.title: Motor da insatisfação, alta no preço dos alimentos é percebida por 72% dos eleitores na Genial/Quaest e pressiona Lula
item.description: The Genial/Quaest poll reveals that 72% of voters perceive rising food prices, which is pressuring President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva's (PT) popularity in his third term. Food inflation, driven by the Middle East war, has reached its highest level under Lula’s government, increasing household debt and voter dissatisfaction. This trend threatens his lead in the October re-election race.

item.title: Na véspera de eleição para presidente da Alerj, PL cogita manter interino enquanto grupo de Paes mira traições
item.description: On the eve of the election for president of Alerj, the PL is considering keeping interim leader Guilherme Delaroli in office, despite the strength of Douglas Ruas as a pre-candidate for state governor, due to legal uncertainties over the succession of the Rio de Janeiro executive. Meanwhile, allies of Eduardo Paes are backing Vitor Junior (PDT) and attempting to lure PL supporters, including probing Delaroli, but are rejected by the party. The Paes strategy also seeks support from PP and Republicans to counterbalance the PL-Unão Brasil-PP alliance backing Ruas.

item.title: Após Datafolha e Quaest, Flávio Bolsonaro supera Lula no 2º turno pela primeira vez no Rali; veja agregador
item.description: The Rali poll aggregator shows, for the first time, Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) leading President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) in a simulated second-round scenario, with 43.3% to 42.6%, reversing Lula’s prior advantage. Lula still leads against Romeu Zema (Novo) and Ronaldo Caiado (PSD), though his margins have narrowed. The Lula government is rated as poor or terrible by 40.8% of the population, while only 31% view it as excellent or good.

item.title: Os 96 milhões que não decidiram em quem votar
item.description: The article highlights the disconnect between most Brazilian voters and the 2026 electoral campaign, exemplified by Valdir, a construction materials store owner in Ribeirão Preto who cares more about how the Copa will boost local sales than national political proposals. Although he thinks about the election, he feels no candidate speaks his language or understands his daily concerns, such as cash flow and local commerce. The piece notes that 96 million voters remain undecided, revealing a deep gap between institutional politics and the real needs of the population.

item.title: 'Cabide de emprego' do crime: afastado dois dias após eleição é o terceiro prefeito seguido de cidade na PB acusado de elo com o CV
item.description: The mayor of Cabedelo, Edvaldo Neto (Avante), was removed from office following a judicial decision over suspicions of involvement in a scheme that may have diverted up to R$ 270 million benefiting members of the criminal faction Tropa do Amigão, a local arm of the Red Command. He is the third consecutive mayor of the city to be targeted by justice over ties to organized crime, continuing a pattern established by his predecessors, Vitor Hugo Castelliano and Andre Coutinho, both from Avante, whose ineligibility was upheld by the TSE in 2024.

item.title: Janja interagia com Choquei, perfil cujo dono foi preso pela PF
item.description: First Lady Janja Lula da Silva interacted with the Choquei profile, owned by Raphael Sousa Oliveira, between July 2022 and October 2023, commenting on posts about Lula and pets. Oliveira was arrested by the Federal Police on April 15, 2026, in Operation Narco Fluxo, suspected of money laundering exceeding R$1.6 billion. Janja has not commented since the arrest, and her last X post was in August 2024.

item.title: Corinthians vence Santa Fé na Libertadores; Flu e Cruzeiro perdem em casa
item.description: Corinthians defeated Independiente Santa Fé 2-0 in the 2026 Copa Libertadores, with goals from Raniel and Gustavo Henrique, topping Group E with six points. Meanwhile, Fluminense lost 2-1 at home to Independiente Rivadavia in a comeback at Maracanã, and Cruzeiro fell 2-1 to Universidad Católica at Mineirão, both unexpected home defeats for Brazilian clubs.

item.title: Como Wagner Moura, veja outros brasileiros que já foram capa da revista Time
item.description: Wagner Moura appeared on the cover of Time magazine in 2024 for his role in 'The Agent,' being named one of the 100 most influential people in the world. Other Brazilians featured on Time's cover include Afrânio do Amaral (1929), Julio Prestes (1930), Getúlio Vargas (1940), Lula (2004, 2010, 2022), Sônia Guajajara (2022), Jânio Quadros (1961), Costa e Silva (1967) and Neymar (regional edition). The list highlights figures from science, politics, sports and indigenous activism.

item.title: 6x1, 5x2, 4x3 e 12x36: como funcionam as principais escalas de trabalho no Brasil
item.description: The Lula government prioritizes ending the 6x1 work scale, submitting a bill to Congress to reduce the weekly workload, while constitutional amendments (PECs) advance in parallel. Experts explain that Brazil’s work schedules — 6x1, 5x2, 4x3, and 12x36 — vary by sector and must respect the 44-hour weekly limit, directly affecting workers’ rest and quality of life.

item.title: Lula: “Trump no tiene derecho a levantarse por la mañana y amenazar a un país”
item.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva criticized former U.S. President Donald Trump's threats against Brazil, stating that no foreign leader has the right to threaten national sovereignty. He emphasized the importance of mutual respect between nations and reaffirmed Brazil's commitment to democracy and independence in foreign policy decisions.

item.title: Erros na regulação do trabalho por aplicativo expõem anacronismo de Lula
item.description: Institutional Relations Minister José Guimarães announced that the regulation of app-based work, a campaign promise by President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, will be postponed 'for later' without specifying a timeline. Despite numerous meetings and debates since the start of his term, the proposal remains stalled due to lack of political consensus and Lula’s own acknowledgment that it is not a good moment to vote on it, according to Deputy Augusto Coutinho.

item.title: Menos carne de paca e mais olho no centro
item.description: Quaest research shows Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) making consistent gains among independent voters, a demographic that will decide the 2026 election — the worst news for the Planalto. Lula’s campaign should pause and shift strategy to counter this trend if it hopes to win. The full article is exclusive to subscribers.

item.title: Escala 6x1: entenda próximos passos após votação em comissão da Câmara ser adiada
item.description: The vote on the bill to end the 6x1 work schedule in Brazil was postponed in the Chamber’s Constitution and Justice Committee to April 22. If approved, it will proceed to a special committee and then the Chamber’s plenary, before undergoing the same process in the Senate. The bill, a key part of Lula’s agenda, seeks to reduce the weekly work limit from 44 to 40 hours, adopting a 5x2 model.

item.title: Câmara deve continuar votação de PEC prevê valor mínimo para assistência social e impacto de R$ 36 bi em 4 anos
item.description: The Chamber of Deputies is set to resume the second-round vote on a Constitutional Amendment Proposal (PEC) establishing a minimum floor of 1% of the Union’s net revenue for the Unified Social Assistance System (Suas), phased in from 0.3% in 2027 to 1% in 2030. The estimated fiscal impact is R$ 36 billion over four years. Following a meeting with the federal government, the Chamber president said the PEC could be voted on Thursday without changes to its core objective.

item.title: Aliados de Ramagem atribuem libertação de ex-deputado nos EUA a integrantes do governo Trump
item.description: Allies of Alexandre Ramagem credited his release from ICE custody in the U.S. to interventions by the Trump administration, including President Donald Trump and Secretary of State Marco Rubio. Ramagem, a fugitive in Brazil after being sentenced by the STF for involvement in the coup plot, was detained in Florida and released two days later without bail, with supporters claiming his immigration status was fully regular. The release was celebrated by Bolsonarist allies, such as Eduardo Bolsonaro and Paulo Figueiredo, who praised the U.S. government’s action as a just response to what they describe as political persecution in Brazil.

item.title: Petrobras faz hoje assembleia de acionistas que deve confirmar novo presidente do seu conselho
item.description: Petrobras holds its Ordinary General Shareholders' Meeting today to reappoint Magda Chambriard as company president and elect a new chair of the Board of Directors, with the federal government nominating Guilherme Mello for the position. The election for 10 board seats features 16 candidates, reflecting partial renewal of nominations and intense competition between government and minority shareholder representatives.

item.title: Vorcaro apresentará proposta de delação só em maio e tensão segue alta em Brasília
item.description: Businessman Daniel Vorcaro has postponed the presentation of his plea bargain proposal until May, which should ease rumors that the deal was imminent. Tension in Brasília remains high amid expectations about the content of the plea bargain and its potential political impact.

item.title: Governo busca condições de aprovar PEC da assistência social
item.description: The Lula administration is pushing to advance PEC 383/2017, which establishes permanent funding for SUAS, aiming to approve it before the 2026 elections. Minister Wellington Dias emphasized the president's full support and the urgency to avoid delays in an election year.

item.title: Lula usa boné pedindo fim da 6 X 1 em reunião com centrais sindicais
item.description: President Lula wore a cap reading 'End the 6x1' during a meeting with trade union leaders at the Palácio do Planalto, advocating for a 40-hour workweek without salary reduction. The government submitted an urgent bill to Congress to abolish the 6x1 work schedule, framing it as a priority for his 2026 re-election bid, and criticized the 2017 labor reform for 'legalizing work precarization'.

item.title: Jabuti da Câmara pode anistiar bolsonaristas que fecharam estradas em 2022
item.description: The Chamber of Deputies approved an urgency request for a bill that includes a rider to pardon truckers aligned with Bolsonaro who blocked highways after the 2022 elections. The rider, unrelated to the bill’s original purpose of forgiving traffic fines for humanitarian aid transporters during the 2024 Rio Grande do Sul floods, seeks to erase fines, civil and administrative sanctions, and ongoing or finalized convictions tied to 2022 protests. Rapporteur Afonso Hamm (PP-RS) argues the measure promotes legal and social pacification.

item.title: Tarcísio nomeia primeira mulher comandante-geral da PM de SP
item.description: São Paulo Governor Tarcísio de Freitas appointed Colonel Glauce Anselmo Cavalli as the first female commander-general of the state's Military Police, breaking nearly two centuries of male dominance in the role. The appointment, announced on April 15, 2026, marks a historic milestone for the institution.

item.title: No Troféu Imprensa, Galvão solta resposta "sincerona" sobre Brasil na Copa. Veja vídeo
item.description: Galvão Bueno, during the Troféu Imprensa recording at SBT, praised the network's initiative to award professionals from different broadcasters and commented on his own trophy collection. Regarding Brazil's chances in the World Cup, he directly stated that what's missing is 'scoring goals,' noting that Brazil is among the favorites alongside France, Spain, and Argentina, the current world champions.

item.title: Senado aprova indicação de Odair Cunha para o TCU
item.description: The Senate approved the appointment of Deputy Odair Cunha (PT-MG) as a minister of the TCU, with 50 votes in favor and 8 against. He will replace retired Minister Aroldo Cedraz, having been nominated by the Chamber of Deputies, which supported him with 303 votes in a vote featuring five candidates. Cunha serves a life term at the TCU and emphasized that the court should guide, not hinder, public management.

item.title: Alcolumbre oferece ajuda a relator da CPI após Gilmar pedir investigação
item.description: Senate President Davi Alcolumbre offered legal support from the Senate's General Counsel to Senator Alessandro Vieira (MDB-SE) after Supreme Court Justice Gilmar Mendes requested an investigation into Vieira. Vieira had sought the indictment of Mendes, Toffoli, Moraes, and Gonet in the Organized Crime CPI, but the motion was rejected. Alcolumbre stated the Senate stands ready to assist legally in defending the legitimacy of the popular vote and senatorial prerogatives.

item.title: Boulos rebate Motta e diz que foi deputado mais votado de SP
item.description: Minister Guilherme Boulos rebutted Chamber President Hugo Motta, who criticized him for a belligerent tone toward Congress during debate on the bill ending the 6x1 work scale. Boulos claimed he was the most voted deputy in São Paulo, asserting his legitimacy to criticize the legislature. The exchange occurred amid discussions on the proposed labor reform.

item.title: Jorge Seif diz que Eduardo Bolsonaro "foi decisivo” para soltura de Ramagem
item.description: Senator Jorge Seif (PL-SC) stated that Eduardo Bolsonaro was decisive in securing the release of Alexandre Ramagem, a former deputy detained by ICE in Orlando, USA. Seif said Eduardo Bolsonaro’s influence with the Trump administration made the difference, calling it the 'first major victory.' He also confirmed filing a political asylum request for Ramagem at the U.S. Embassy in Brasília.

item.title: Caiado diz ser favorável ao impeachment ‘de quem quer que seja’
item.description: Ronaldo Caiado (PSD), former governor of Goiás and presidential pre-candidate, stated he supports the impeachment of 'whoever it may be,' including the president, STF ministers, and other public officials, while arguing that presidential candidates should not enjoy the presumption of innocence. He reaffirmed his pledge to sign a broad, general, and unrestricted amnesty on his first day in office for those convicted in the January 8 attacks, including Jair Bolsonaro.

item.title: Câmara acelera projeto que pode anistiar bolsonaristas que bloquearam estradas após eleições de 2022
item.description: The Chamber of Deputies approved the urgent processing of a bill that amnesties traffic violations committed by drivers involved in humanitarian aid following floods in Rio Grande do Sul. However, the bill includes a rider (jabuti) that also amnesties truckers who participated in blockades and protests in 2022, many of whom were linked to Bolsonarist acts contesting the election results. The measure is controversial as it may benefit individuals involved in actions deemed anti-democratic.

item.title: Lula critica reforma trabalhista e chama Bolsonaro de ‘a coisa que veio depois do Temer’
item.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva criticized the 2017 labor reform approved by Michel Temer, calling it responsible for the precarization of work and social security. During a meeting with trade union centrals, Lula also referred to Jair Bolsonaro as 'the thing that came after Temer', accusing both of deepening attacks on labor rights and democratic institutions.

item.title: Alexandre Ramagem é solto após ficar dois dias preso nos EUA
item.description: Former federal deputy and ex-Abin director Alexandre Ramagem was released on Wednesday, March 15, after being detained for two days in the United States, where he is a fugitive from Brazilian justice over his role in the 2022 coup plot. He was arrested on Monday, March 13, by ICE agents in Orlando, Florida. Ramagem fled Brazil in September 2023 using an unretained diplomatic passport and has had his congressional mandate revoked by the Chamber of Deputies.

item.title: STF asfixia debate sobre justiça do trabalho, diz Luiz Marinho
item.description: Labor Minister Luiz Marinho accused the STF of stifling the debate on labor pejotization by claiming labor courts lack jurisdiction, warning of legal insecurity. He and President Lula urged discussion of the Workers' Agenda, including ending pejotization and the 6x1 work scale, in a meeting with union leaders at the Planalto Palace.

item.title: Por que Gilmar Mendes pediu à PGR para investigar relator da CPI do Crime Organizado
item.description: Supreme Court Justice Gilmar Mendes has asked the Prosecutor General's Office (PGR) to investigate Senator Alessandro Vieira (MDB-SE) for abuse of authority, following Vieira's report in the Organized Crime CPI that recommended indicting three STF ministers and the PGR over responsibility crimes. Mendes argued the CPI lacked jurisdiction, as its mandate covers organized crime, not responsibility crimes, and accused Vieira of using a 'juvenile wordplay' to overstep his authority. The report was rejected by the CPI in a 6-4 vote.

item.title: Câmara aprova projeto que reconhece a atividade circense como manifestação da cultura brasileira
item.description: The Chamber of Deputies approved a bill recognizing circus activity as a manifestation of Brazilian popular culture and art nationwide. The proposal, originating from the Senate and reported by Deputy Capitão Augusto (PL-SP), will be sent for presidential sanction. The rapporteur emphasized the circus's itinerant and democratic role in cultural diffusion, tradition preservation, and social inclusion.

item.title: Motta alinha cronograma para acelerar PEC do fim da escala 6×1
item.description: Following Lula’s submission of a constitutional urgency bill on workweek reduction, Chamber President Hugo Motta coordinated with party leaders to prioritize the PEC ending the 6×1 work schedule. Extra sessions on Thursday and Friday will allow the CCJ to review the proposal next week, aiming for approval in both committee and plenary by end of May.

item.title: Lula diz a sindicatos para cobrarem Gilmar Mendes por fim da pejotização
item.description: President Lula (PT) urged labor unions to pressure Supreme Court Justice Gilmar Mendes to act against labor 'pejotização' — a form of outsourced work he says harms the country. Mendes, who is the rapporteur on a case regarding employment contracts, has a history of rulings favorable to maintaining the practice. The statement was made on April 15, 2026, at 9:03 PM.

item.title: A crise entre os poderes, com STF e Executivo unidos, está escalando
item.description: The STF and the Executive are united in a failed attempt to restore institutional legitimacy, but this alliance is deepening the crisis between powers. The Court faces internal divisions, with one faction advocating institutional rigidity as fatal, while another ignores the political impact of eroding credibility. The attempt to indict justices via CPI reflects public perception of the STF as a symbol of an intolerable system, and the Court’s hardline reactions are fueling greater resistance in Congress and society, increasing the risk of civil disobedience.

item.title: Ministro do STJ critica interferência em ações e diz que 'todo mundo está vendendo voto'
item.description: Minister João Otávio de Noronha of the Superior Tribunal of Justice (STJ) criticized external interference in ongoing court cases, stating that 'Brasília is very difficult' and that 'everyone is selling votes around, all over Brazil'. He emphasized the severity of the situation during a session of the Fourth Panel of the tribunal.

item.title: Lula pede mobilização a centrais sindicais para fim da escala 6x1
item.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva received 68 demands from union representatives after sending to Congress a bill to reduce the workweek to 40 hours (ending the 6x1 schedule), urging workers to mobilize for its approval. Lula emphasized the need for union pressure, criticized the 2017 Labor Reform and 2019 Pension Reform as setbacks, and honored activist Rick Azevedo, who inspired the bill after experiencing burnout. The event also warned against opposition proposals to increase work hours, similar to those in Argentina.

item.title: Projetos de renaturalização de rios avançam no Brasil para combater enchentes
item.description: River renaturalization projects are advancing in Brazil, with initiatives in São Paulo (Tietê, Pinheiros, Bixiga Creek), Rio de Janeiro (Limpa Rio Margens), and Piauí (Parnaíba basin), signaling a paradigm shift from rigid containment to ecological recovery and multifunctional use. These efforts combine drainage, sanitation, riverside redevelopment, and public access, highlighted by a R$9 billion PPP slated for auction in 2026 and the Integra Tietê program aiming to cut organic load by 54% by 2029.

item.title: Ramagem ganha liberdade nos EUA após 2 dias de detenção
item.description: Former federal deputy Alexandre Ramagem (PL-RJ) was released on Wednesday (15) after two days of detention by U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) in Florida. He had fled Brazil in September 2025 to avoid serving a 16-year sentence for his role in the 2022 coup plot, using a diplomatic passport irregularly. His release comes as Brazil's extradition request awaits a response from the U.S. government.

item.title: Lula critica o fim do imposto sindical
item.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva criticized the abolition of the union tax, which was eliminated by the 2017 labor reform, claiming the previous government financially strangled unions while business owners retained privileges like the S System. He made the remarks during a meeting with union centrals to deliver the Workers' Class Agenda, which includes 68 demands for 2026–2030, such as reducing the workweek without cutting wages and ending the 6X1 schedule. The government also sent an urgent bill to Congress to abolish the 6X1 work schedule, coinciding with the Workers' Class March in Brasília.

item.title: 'Foram dias duros', diz mulher de Ramagem após soltura de ex-diretor da Abin nos EUA pelo ICE
item.description: The wife of Alexandre Ramagem, Rebeca Ramagem, released a video after her husband's release by ICE agents in the U.S., describing his detention as 'hard days, of pain and injustice' and alleging persecution. She reiterated her support for pre-candidate Flávio Bolsonaro, while allies credited the release to the Trump administration, though U.S. authorities did not confirm the detention stemmed from a minor traffic violation.

item.title: A troca de farpas entre Gilmar Mendes e Romeu Zema
item.description: Supreme Court Justice Gilmar Mendes rebutted criticisms from former Minas Gerais governor Romeu Zema, who had labeled the court 'corrupt' and called for the removal and arrest of justices. Mendes highlighted the contradiction in Zema's stance, noting that the former governor benefited from STF rulings that suspended Minas Gerais' debt payments to the Union—estimated at R$ 165 billion—but now attacks the Court when its decisions oppose his political interests.

item.title: Lula critica ‘pejotização’ e pede reunião de centrais sindicais com Gilmar Mendes
item.description: President Lula criticized pejotization in a meeting with union leaders, stating that the practice of hiring workers as legal entities harms employees, Social Security, FGTS, and public housing and sanitation policies. He urged unions to schedule a meeting with Supreme Court Minister Gilmar Mendes, who is the rapporteur of a case assessing the constitutionality of pejotization, to expose its harms. Lula also attacked the labor and pension reforms of Temer and Bolsonaro, claiming they 'buried' workers' rights.

item.title: Ramagem é solto nos EUA 2 dias após ser preso pelo ICE
item.description: Alexandre Ramagem, former head of Brazil's intelligence agency Abin and sentenced to 16 years in prison by the STF for coup attempt, was detained by ICE in the U.S. on April 13, 2026, and released two days later, according to Paulo Figueiredo and Eduardo Bolsonaro. He had been a fugitive since his conviction, with the crimes committed while holding public office.

item.title: Governo Lula piora trajetória de projeção da dívida até 2035
item.description: Brazil's general government gross debt (DBGG) is now projected to reach 87.8% of GDP in 2029, up from the previous forecast of 84.2% peaking in 2028, according to the Ministry of Finance. The debt-to-GDP ratio rose from 71.7% at the end of 2022 to 79.2% in February 2025, driven by high interest rates (Selic), persistent primary deficits, and rising public spending. The exclusion of R$ 347 billion in precatory payments from the primary surplus target until 2035, as proposed in the new LDO, was cited as a key factor worsening the debt trajectory between 2025 and 2026.
